Nashville Farmers’ Market—2013-2014 TAEP Grant Application The Nashville Farmers’ Market (NFM) is operated by the Metropolitan Government of Nashville & Davidson County and opened at Its current location In 1995. The Farmers’ Market facility covers over 16 acres of urban land and is composed of a 38,000 square foot Interior, enclosed “Market House,” flanked by four covered exterior retail sheds, each measuring about 15,000 square feet. The Market House is climate-controlled and exterior sheds are open-air w/convertible tarps. All flooring is concrete. NFM is fully handicap-accessible and has only one permanent sign (a Rosa L. Parks Blvd, electronic marquee), - We have over 300 free parking spaces and nine restrooms In our footprint. NEM is openseverr days a week; 362-daysayear. The Farmers’ Market an {nterlm Director, Marketing Director, Grow Local Kitchen Director, Officer, and two maintenance/janitorial team members. NFM receives oversight & governance support from Nashville Farmers’ Market Board whose members are appointed by the Mayor that Includes; a Davidson County farmer & rancher, three Davidson County restaurant owners, and other community members. The organizational goal of NFM in 2014 Is to continue our efforts towards becoming the Southeast’s premier farmers market & Tennessee’s central source & retail outlet for farmers, artisans, & crafters throughout all seasons, - Depending on the season, the Market hosts over 200 merchants. The NFM Farm sheds provide 96 spaces reserved for retailing produce, locally-made foods, farm products, and plant material. Throughout the growing season It Is home to over 60 farmers, 40 artisans, and up to 10 resellers, Prime . space allocation is reserved-for jocal4armers, selling their own products, food:producers who make their own foods In commercial or certified domestic kitchens. In 2013 (& w/assistance from _. TAEP funds) NFM “zoned” shed areas to Include; all of Shed 2 as a “Producers-Only Shed,” and half of Shed-1 as a “Farmer-Only farmers coming to NFM multiple days (versus only) received prime space allocation. A third North Shed also became NFIV’s “Plant & Crafter Shed” to accommodate plant/nursery farms & a growing number of non-food crafters making local products. In total, the Market reserved 148 shed spaces (3/4 of Market Shed space) solely for farmers, artisans, and crafters In 2013. In 2011, NFM opened up interior Market House space to accommodate up to 20 artisans & crafters and this has contInued—farmers also may select this space option In any season. In 2012, we opened NFM’s Grow Local inside the The Grow Local Kitchen Is a fully certified & licensed kitchen available for production rental, culinary education classes, “pop-up” restaurant rental, & catering services made with farm-fresh & local Ingredients. Over 2013, the number of producers using Grow Local Kitchen has doubled & we expect It to triple in 2014. We are also proud to share that in 2013, through Internal efforts; we Increased the permanent restaurants/shops inside The Market House using farm produce-or-product in-daity menus/operations from six to ten fourteen total), and plan to strive for 100% during peak season in 2014. Some farmers are small production farmers and visit the Market one or two days per week. Specialty- crop farmers may retail thelr product seven days a week while thelr product fs In season. Other farmers ARCHIVE
have large enough production to sell thelr product at the Market throughout the growing season. Over the past 5 years, we have increased the numbers of farmers and artisans selling directly to the public from an average of 4 to over 60 in peak season. Since the Market is open year-round, there are up to 10 resale,merchants that.sell every.day at the Market. They purchase their products from produce houses during-the local season. Currently, resellers occupy 25% of the south farm shed area. NFM has also engaged In its fifth year of Vanderbllt Market featuring 20 local farmers & artisans (an Increase from 12 In previous years) as a one-day “pop up” market In the heart of Vanderbilt's Plaza. NFM also continues to work to Increase selling opportunities and community engagement through Night Markets, expanded shopping hours, community outreach, & seeking additional partnership opportunities. Our Market Is currently promoted via some advertising, website, events, outreach, e-newsletter, and ‘through social media. © In previous TAEP grant submissions-we described many of our as a multi-year project in © process.. In 2014, hoping to complete and enhance these Initiatives based on what learned. Over 2013, we have developed a five-year strategic plan in partnership with NFM’s, Board, merchants, and customers. Through this planning process, NFM has been solidly preparing & activating upon efforts to further Increase the presence of farmers, artisans, & merchants committed to “growing local” evermore than ever before. In the past, customers clearly told us they wanted to know; what they are buying, where it comes from, . how much that they want more variety, expanded shopping hours;more-classes& education-via in-Market events, website, e-letter, & soclal media interaction. Over the last four years (& with TAEP grant assistance). we have made great strides In all of these areas. We have; created a new signage program that color-codes & defines sourcing & pricing; worked with our farmers:to-grow continued Night Markets; conducted more'classes & events; launched 2 new websites (one dedicated to Grow Local Kitchen by our Grow Local Kitchen Director); expanded our use & regularity of media & e-letter interactions; worked to tell the story of the Market, the “faces behind the food” of our farmers & artisans, and entice & inspire purchasing through branding redesigns & recipe promotions; increased the presence of seasonality charts & information both online & in print; and conducted _ Interactive demos with groups of all ages. Over 2013, worked to Incorporate Grow Local Kitchen into peak season more fully by; renting to local producers for product-making and/or “pop up” restaurants, offering unique classes & events, and providing catering services using Market farmers, artisans, and merchants. This has been successful and we graclously request the opportunity to take many of these key initiatives to a heightened level. In 2013, to great success; critical banners & signage pieces, convertible artwork letting the public know where to find those who grow it, make It, bake it, craft It, etc, in line with our expanded allocation plan.
